articles.title: Super League: Huddersfield Giants thrash Castleford Tigers in Accu Stadium swansong
articles.summary: Huddersfield signed off from the Accu Stadium with a morale-boosting 48-16 win over Castleford in the final game of the regular Betfred Super League season.
articles.body:
Huddersfield Giants put on a show for the fans, running over eight tries against Castleford Tigers, in an emotional farewell after 32 years at their home ground; watch the Super League play-offs from September 18, live on Sky Sports, with Grand Final on October 3

Huddersfield signed off from the Accu Stadium with a morale-boosting 48-16 win over Castleford in the final game of the regular Betfred Super League season.

Taane Milne and Jacob Gagai both scored twice as the Giants cruised to victory, made all the more impressive by the first-half dismissal of Fenton Rogers for leading with the elbow.

But it meant more misery for the woeful visitors, who slipped below their opponents into 13th place after a dismal run of just one win in their last eight games.

Milne marked his final appearance for the Giants with the opening try, and although Liam Hood hit back for Castleford, three tries in 10 minutes from Tristan Powell, Connor Wrench and Gagai put Huddersfield firmly in control at 24-6 by half-time.

Even Rogers' dismissal just before the interval for his challenge on Tyler Dupree could not gift the under-par Tigers a route back into the contest.

They did raise a flicker of hope when Daejarn Asi jinked through a static Giants defence to score the first try after the restart, with Ben McNamara's second conversion edging them closer.

But a penalty from Tui Lolohea, who also kicked five conversions in his final game for the club, followed by further tries from Zac Woolford and Gagai's second, confirmed an impressive Giants victory.

It also marked the end of the Giants' long association with the Accu Stadium under its various names, with the RFL having ratified the club's move to Dewsbury Rams' 5,100-capacity Flair Stadium from next season.

articles.title: La confesión de George Russell tras probar el Mercedes más salvaje: se arrepiente de no comprarlo... aunque era por una buena razón
articles.standfirst: El británico pudo conducir el impactante Mercedes-AMG CLE 646... y quizá sea una de las pocas veces que pueda hacerlo
articles.summary: El británico pudo conducir el impactante Mercedes-AMG CLE 646... y quizá sea una de las pocas veces que pueda hacerlo
articles.body: Entre los actos que han protagonizado los pilotos oficiales del equipo Mercedes AMG de F1 en el Gran Premio de España hubo uno que llamó especialmente la atención: la presentación mundial del impresionante Mercedes-AMG CLE 646... en la Plaza de Toros de Las Ventas. En el coso madrileño, la capital mundial del toreo, Kimi Antonelli y George Russell pudieron contemplar en todo su esplendor una de las máquinas más extremas con el logo de la estrella en su carrocería: un coupé de dos plazas, con 646 caballos de potencia y una imagen tan extrema como sugerente. Un súper deportivo que, aunque no ha rodado por La Monumental (la curva más icónica del circuito de Madring) sí que lo hizo por el albero de 'la otra' Monumental en una puesta en escena impresionante y muy especial. Y aprovechando que una de las 30 unidades que se fabricarán de este Mercedes tan especial estaba en Madrid... qué mejor que entregarla a sus pilotos de Fórmula 1 para que lucieran por la capital de España. Hoy, la marca alemana le ha entregado las llaves del CLE 646 a George Russell. El británico, por supuesto, no sólo no rechazó la invitación sino que le sacó partido en su camino a Madring... haciendo rugir el V8 biturbo cada vez que podía (incluido en los túneles de la capital). Incluso, y sin quererlo, llegó a hacer patinar las ruedas traseras (es un deportivo de propulsión) en alguna arrancada. Y arriesgó un poco acelerando con fuerza en las inmediaciones de IFEMA... delante de la policía española: "Se han quedado mirando", decía entre risas (y menos mal que hicieron eso y no se lanzaron a por él...). Pero lo más curioso llegó al final del vídeo, cuando Russell confesó algo sorprendente: "Creo que me estoy arrepintiendo de no comprar uno de estos cuando me lo ofrecieron", soltó, para sorpresa de todos los que hayan visto el vídeo... incluidos nosotros. Porque un coche como este, con sólo 30 unidades para todo el mundo, es un valor seguro (aparte de la diversión que pueda ofrecer cada vez que lo saques de paseo, como el propio Russell pudo comprobar). Sin embargo... había un par de buenas razones para ello (o, al menos, dos excusas). "En ese momento me estaba comprando un apartamento... y un anillo de bodas", justifica (recordemos que recientemente contrajo matrimonio con la española Carmen Montero Mundt). Y no creemos que sea porque el precio del Mercedes-AMG CLE 646 sea inalcanzable para Russell y su millonario salario (a nosotros la marca alemana no nos lo ha revelado, pero seguro que su piloto sí lo sabe)... incluso con sus otros gastos añadidos. Pero lo que es seguro es que ahora va a tener difícil conseguir uno... porque todos están ya asignados.

images.caption: George Russell y el Mercedes-AMG GLE 646 Mercedes-Benz

articles.title: Ariela Sánchez, bronce en el Grand Slam de Budapest
articles.standfirst: Supera a la eslovena Kaja Kajze para lograr su primera medalla en un evento de este categoría
articles.summary: Supera a la eslovena Kaja Kajze para lograr su primera medalla en un evento de este categoría
articles.body: Ariela Sánchez se colgó el bronce (-63 kilos) en el Grand Slam de Budapest de judo. Tras el oro conseguido por Ayumi Leiva en -52 kg, la delegación española sumó su segunda medalla en esta competición. Tras caer en semifinales ante la eslovena Kaja Kajzer, la pupila de Sugoi Uriarte se repuso para llevarse el combate por el bronce ante la austríaca Lubjana Piovesana por ippon. Antes había logrado imponerse a la rumana Amanda Zuaznabar-Totres en primera ronda, a la croata Iva Oberan en octavos y a la polaca Natalia Kropska en cuartos. Ariela Sánchez, de origen dominicano y que superó una grave peritonitis en 2023, logra así su primera medalla en un Grand Slam. Este año había pisado ya el tercer peldaño del podio en el Open Europeo de Liubliana y en el de Varsovia.

images.caption: Ariela Sánchez, de azul, durante su combate ante Lubjana Piovesana. G. Sabau/E.Di Feliciantonio (IFJ)

articles.title: Top OHL Prospect Tanner Adams Traded for 17 Draft Picks in Blockbuster Steelheads-Wolves Deal
articles.summary: Tanner Adams is still two years away from being NHL-draft eligible, but the hype around the 16-year-old prospect is already strong enough that he brought back 17 draft picks in an OHL trade on Friday night.
articles.body:
Tanner Adams is still two years away from being NHL-draft eligible, but the hype around the 16-year-old prospect is already strong enough that he brought back 17 draft picks in an OHL trade on Friday night.

Two months after the Brampton Steelheads selected Adams with the No. 3 pick in the 2026 OHL draft, they flipped him to the Sudbury Wolves for a package of 17 picks from 2027 to '30.

Sudbury is technically only giving up 15 picks with the other two coming from the OHL, including a comp pick that will be No. 5 overall in the 2027 draft.

The trade appears to have been part of a strategic play from Brampton's side.

Per The Athletic's Scott Wheeler , it was "widely known" before the draft that Sudbury was Adams' preferred destination in part because it's the closest OHL team to his hometown.

Since the Wolves didn't make their first pick until No. 5, Brampton grabbed Adams two picks before they went on the clock. The Steelheads turned it into a cache of future selections they can use to build their roster going forward.

Sudbury, meanwhile, will be hoping Adams can provide a boost for the 2026-27 season. It finished last year as the No. 8 seed in the Eastern Conference and was swept by the Brantford Bulldogs in the first round of the playoffs.

articles.title: Jey Uso Responds to WWE Fans Taunting Him With Chants During South American Tour
articles.summary: Jey Uso clapped back at fans Saturday after their negative reactions toward him during WWE's live event tour of South America.
articles.body:
Jey Uso clapped back at fans Saturday after their negative reactions toward him during WWE's live event tour of South America.

In a post on his Instagram Stories (h/t WrestlePurists), Uso wrote, "Yo South America, disrespect me uno mas [again], I'll go home."

On Saturday night, Jey teamed with Jimmy Uso and Jacob Fatu in a losing effort against Seth Rollins, Solo Sikoa and LA Knight in a six-man tag team match in Buenos Aires, Argentina, per Matt Boone of WrestlingHeadlines.com.

According to WrestlePurists , fans chanted, "You can't wrestle," at the one-time world heavyweight champion and Royal Rumble winner.

While The Bloodline is somewhat undefined in terms of whether it is a heel or babyface stable, Jey and Co. have undoubtedly had some villainous tendencies in recent weeks and months.

Most notably, they attacked Sikoa on the Aug. 17 episode of Raw, and they have been at odds with Knight, both of whom are hugely popular babyfaces currently.

Because of that, the South American fans showing their displeasure with Jey and The Bloodline works with what WWE is trying to accomplish.

That also opened the door for Jey to be an antagonist on social media, which could help him garner even more heat with the fans moving forward.

articles.title: Leeds United Player Face FA Ban Threat Clash: Could The Whites Cope Without Him?
articles.summary: Leeds United could face an FA disciplinary headache after an off-the-ball clash involving their 29-year-old midfielder Harry Wilson during Wednesday’s Caraba...
articles.body:
Leeds United could face an FA disciplinary headache after an off-the-ball clash involving their 29-year-old midfielder Harry Wilson during Wednesday's Carabao Cup defeat at Stamford Bridge. According to a report published on September 10 by Kwadwo Hemeng for The Leeds Press , the midfielder appeared to catch Chelsea 's Valentín Barco on the back of the head with his knee as he went to retrieve the ball for a throw-in. Referee Jarred Gillett stepped in and calmed the situation, yet he showed no card.

The incident escaped an in-game review because VAR was unavailable for this stage of the competition. That leaves the FA with scope to examine the footage and decide whether the contact amounts to violent conduct. A disciplinary panel could impose a suspension if it considers the action worthy of punishment. The report comes after Chelsea overturned Leeds ' early advantage in a 6-3 victory, with the visitors collapsing after the interval.

Could Leeds United cope without their midfielder?

A ban would hurt Leeds United at a bad time, because the club still have plenty to repair after conceding six goals and letting a promising cup display unravel. Wilson gives Daniel Farke a useful creative outlet from midfield, and his passing, set-piece delivery and ability to move the ball through pressure give the manager a different option when matches become tight.

LEEDS, ENGLAND – AUGUST 30: Harry Wilson of Leeds in action during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Leeds United and Brentford at Elland Road on August 30, 2026 in Leeds, England. (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images)

That loss of variety matters. Take Wilson out for several games, and Farke has to alter his midfield balance by changing personnel or asking another player to carry more creative responsibility. With a domestic schedule demanding regular rotation, suspension could leave the squad thinner and reduce Farke's room to protect tired players without weakening the side.

Then comes the less measurable damage. Leeds United had spent much of the first half putting Chelsea under pressure, only to watch the contest swing violently afterwards. A disciplinary case would drag attention away from the football and place another question in front of Farke when he needs the group focused on defensive discipline and recovery.

Why could Leeds United feel the fallout so sharply?

Leeds United can't afford that noise. Six conceded at Stamford Bridge already gives critics plenty to discuss; losing a key midfielder because of an avoidable incident would add another line to the story. Farke needs players who stay switched on after a collapse of this size, and a retrospective suspension would make selection harder just as the next league fixture arrives. Losing a valuable midfield piece would leave the manager trying to restore confidence, defensive order and control.

articles.title: Which Bucs wideouts should you start in fantasy week 1?
articles.summary: Jalen McMillan's likely absence could create more fantasy opportunities for the rest of the Bucs' receiving corps against Cincinnati.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers enter Week 1 with plenty of weapons for Baker Mayfield, but the wide receiver room isn't completely healthy heading into Sunday's matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals . Jalen McMillan is doubtful with a knee injury, making it unlikely Tampa Bay will have its usual top three receivers together. Emeka Egbuka appears ready to go after dealing with a toe injury, while Chris Godwin enters the opener healthy.

McMillan's expected absence could also create an opportunity for Ted Hurst III, who sits behind him on the depth chart. Here's how fantasy managers should approach Tampa Bay's receivers in Week 1.

Godwin should be one of the easier decisions for fantasy managers. He enters the season healthy after injuries disrupted his 2025 campaign, and his established connection with Mayfield gives him a solid floor in Tampa Bay's passing game.

McMillan's likely absence could make Godwin even more relied on than planned. Tampa Bay still has Egbuka, Cade Otton, and others as options in the passing game, but taking one starting receiver out of the equation leaves opportunities available elsewhere. Godwin's ability to work underneath and from the slot also gives Mayfield an experienced target if Cincinnati's revamped defensive front forces him to get the ball out quickly.

Egbuka's toe was worth monitoring in preseason and earlier in the week, but his practice participation has taken away much of the concern heading into Sunday. The second-year receiver was a full participant throughout the week and enters the matchup without an injury designation.

That's especially important with McMillan doubtful for Week 1's contest against the Bengals. Egbuka was already going to have a significant role in the offense, and there could be more opportunities available if Tampa Bay is forced to shuffle its receiver rotation. Cincinnati does have talent in its secondary, particularly DJ Turner II, so the matchup shouldn't be treated as an automatic breakout spot, but Egbuka's health and expected role make him a receiver fantasy managers can comfortably keep in their lineups.

Hurst becomes a much more interesting option if McMillan is inactive. The rookie is listed behind McMillan on Tampa Bay's depth chart and could be asked to handle a larger role in his NFL debut, but an increase in snaps doesn't necessarily guarantee enough targets to make him a dependable fantasy option.

Godwin and Egbuka remain ahead of him in the passing game, while Irving, Gainwell, and Otton give Mayfield other established options. That makes Hurst more of a desperation play for managers in deeper leagues or those already dealing with injuries at receiver. Still, McMillan's expected absence gives him a path to immediate playing time, and his usage Sunday will be worth monitoring for more than just Week 1.

McMillan being listed as doubtful makes this the easiest decision of the group. The knee injury limited him throughout the week, and even an unexpected active designation Sunday wouldn't make him a safe fantasy option because there is too much uncertainty surrounding his potential workload.

Fantasy managers should keep McMillan on the bench and see how Tampa Bay handles his return before putting him back into a lineup. His status also directly affects Hurst, who could become the primary beneficiary if McMillan is inactive against Cincinnati.

For Week 1, Godwin and Egbuka are the Tampa Bay receivers fantasy managers can trust, while Hurst is a high-risk option for managers searching deeper into their benches. McMillan should remain out of lineups until his knee is ready and Tampa Bay establishes what his role will look like when he returns.

articles.title: Texas student wins $1.2M on College GameDay, donates half to charity
articles.summary: University of Texas student from Indiana kicked a field goal on ESPN College GameDay and won $1.2 million. He has promised to donate half to charity.
articles.body:
ESPN College GameDay was very profitable for one University of Texas student. Each Week on the pregame show, former kicker Pat McAfee picks one student to take part in his Kicking is Easy field goal contest. This week, he picked Connor Kacena-Merrell from Zionsville, Indiana. And Matthew McConnaghey was on hand to help.

The Texas student from the Indianapolis-area complimented McAfee on his philanthropic efforts and said he enjoyed watching McAfee and new Pro Football Hall of Famer Adam Vinatieri at Lucas Oil Stadium, home of the Colts.

The freshman also said he would donate half his winnings to Building Tomorrow , an Indianapolis-based non-profit organization that works with communities in East Africa to give children access to quality education.

Kacena-Merrell had plenty of leg in his first attempt, but pulled it just a little bit wide right. McConnaghey and ESPN College GameDay's Kirk Herbstreit each promised to add $100,000 to the pot and gave Kacena-Merrell a second chance. Kacena-Merrell took advantage.

The UT student booted a strong kick right down the middle to win $1.2 million dollars. No matter what happens at the Texas-Ohio State game tonight, it was a great day for the young man from Indiana.

Kacena-Merrell didn't play football in high school, but he did play volleyball at Park Tudor High School and youth soccer.

articles.title: Chelsea boss Alonso for yearns for 'boring game' after Hull make their point
articles.summary: Xabi Alonso admitted he would love Chelsea to give him a "boring game" after their defensive woes allowed Hull to escape Stamford Bridge with a 2-2 draw on S...
articles.body:
Xabi Alonso admitted he would love Chelsea to give him a "boring game" after their defensive woes allowed Hull to escape Stamford Bridge with a 2-2 draw on Saturday.

Alonso's side were cruising after Morgan Rogers drilled home in the seventh minute, but once again they paid the price for some sloppy defending.

Hull's Algerian winger Mohamed Belloumi blasted the equaliser after Chelsea failed to clear a long ball.

And Belloumi put the tireless Tigers in front when his deflected shot flashed in before half-time.

Cole Palmer 's incisive run and cut-back in the 66th minute allowed Joao Pedro to bag Chelsea's equaliser.

But the Blues couldn't find a winner and have now conceded nine goals in their four Premier League matches this season.

They also shipped three goals against Leeds in midweek but ran out 6-3 winners in the League Cup third round tie.

That chaotic clash encapsulated Chelsea under Alonso, who was hired in the close season to improve their fortunes after last term's disappointing 10th place finish.

The Spaniard is well aware that Chelsea's attacking quality, which has brought 10 goals in four league games, is being dented by their issues in defence.

"Maybe entertaining, but I hope one day you'll say it was a boring game and we win and we don't give these entertaining moments," Alonso said.

"It kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to fix them.

"When we get the lead, you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially for the first goal. We can do much better. It was too soft.

"That momentum that we had (was lost), it changed the mood. It's something we need to keep talking (about) and address. We will get better, but it's having an impact on our performances."

Chelsea have been highly entertaining in the season's early weeks but their inability to control matches has become a concern.

Hull could have been out of sight had Emiliano Martinez not recovered from a fumble to clear the danger as Oli McBurnie looked poised to make it 3-1.

"Overall I think that we are attacking better than defending," said Alonso.

"It's a big topic and a big theme for us. It's just four games, but the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don't like it.

"We can do better for sure. When we have the lead, a very important part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distances. I'm sure that we can do better."

articles.title: Emery explains Aston Villa striker’s half-time substitution in Nottingham Forest loss
articles.summary: Unai Emery has revealed Nicolas Jackson was substituted at half-time against Nottingham Forest because he feared the striker could be sent off.Jackson had al...
articles.body:
Unai Emery has revealed Nicolas Jackson was substituted at half-time against Nottingham Forest because he feared the striker could be sent off.

Jackson had already been booked during the first half, with Emery saying the referee warned him that the forward needed to be careful following further incidents.

The Villa boss subsequently decided not to take any risks and replaced Jackson at the interval.

"Nico Jackson had a yellow card and the referee was telling us that he needed to keep calm," Emery explained after the 2-1 defeat.

"If not, he was close to having another yellow card. I know Jackson and he could have one action with his power being dangerous for another yellow.

Meanwhile, Emery says Ian Maatsen's injury looks a bad one , while Pau Torres has suffered a hamstring injury.

articles.summary: The No. 17 SMU Mustangs (1-0) come back on a short week to host the UC Davis Aggies (2-0), ranked sixth in the FCS Coaches Poll, in their home opener in Dall...
articles.body:
The No. 17 SMU Mustangs (1-0) come back on a short week to host the UC Davis Aggies (2-0), ranked sixth in the FCS Coaches Poll, in their home opener in Dallas on Saturday.

Jan 2, 2026; San Diego, CA, USA; SMU Mustangs quarterback Kevin Jennings (7) throws the ball against the Arizona Wildcats in the first half during the Holiday Bowl at Snapdragon Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images

SMU outlasted a nearly two-hour delay due to a power outage to beat Florida State 27-24 on Monday night in Tallahassee, Florida. Nick Reed booted a 20-yard field goal with 21 seconds left for the winning score after Kevin Jennings shook off two interceptions to throw for 430 yards and three touchdowns in the Atlantic Coast Conference matchup. Yannick Smith caught five passes for 107 yards and a 79-yard score while Randy Pittman Jr. and Jalen Cooper also caught TD passes. Kendrick Raphael led the ground game with 75 yards on 12 carries.

UC Davis plays its third straight road game after cruising to a 49-17 win last Saturday at San Diego. After trailing 7-0 early, the Aggies put up 28 points in the second quarter as Treynor Cleeland finished 22-of-31 for 294 yards and five touchdowns with an interception. Samuel Gbatu Jr. caught nine balls for 129 yards and two scores while Matteo Perez ran for 123 yards and a touchdown on just nine carries. Jordan Fisher scored two TDs, one on the ground to go with a touchdown reception, and Edward Khutsishvili and Tyler Hennessey also made scoring grabs.

Saturday marks the first meeting between the programs. The Mustangs finished 9-4 last season, including a 6-2 record in the ACC, and beat Arizona in the Holiday Bowl. The Aggies also went 9-4, falling to Illinois State in the FCS playoff quarterfinals.

articles.title: Charlotte Hornets Starters’ Stats Predictions for 2026-27
articles.summary: Charlotte Hornets starters’ stats predictions for 2026-27 are genuinely difficult — because this is a starting five that has never played a regular-season ga...
articles.body:
Charlotte Hornets starters' stats predictions for 2026-27 are genuinely difficult — because this is a starting five that has never played a regular-season game together.

New faces, new roles, new expectations. Coby White steps up as the primary point guard. Brandon Miller carries the offense as the undisputed first option for the first time. Kon Knueppel enters year two with the whole league prepared for him. Naz Reid, who joins from Minnesota , and Moussa Diabate anchor the frontcourt.

Five players, five different storylines. Here is how the numbers might actually land.

White averaged 15.6 points, 3.0 assists, 39.1% from three in 19.3 minutes off the bench over 21 appearances off the bench. As a starter in Chicago before that, he averaged 18.6 points and 4.7 assists in 29 minutes a game. The bench role understated him. Now he projects to see 30-plus minutes as Charlotte's starting point guard every night.

Prediction: 20.6 points, 6.0 assists, 4.0 rebounds, 38.5% from three

White's scoring is consistent, and his playmaking has always looked better with a real role than in a reduced one. Six assists per game feels right for a player getting the keys for the first time. The three-point percentage dips slightly as he takes more off-the-dribble shots, but the volume stays high enough to keep him dangerous.

Knueppel averaged 18.5 points, 5.3 rebounds, 3.4 assists, 42.5% from three — the most three-pointers made by a rookie in NBA history — last season. The challenge heading into year two is that defenses have watched every second of that tape and will contest harder, deny earlier and dare him to create off the dribble rather than catching in rhythm.

Prediction: 20.5 points, 5.5 rebounds, 4.0 assists, 40.5% from three

Without LaMelo Ball feeding him the perfect pass before defenses close out, his three-point percentage dips — but the increased usage and expanded role push his scoring higher. The four assists per game projection reflects a player being asked to create more for himself and others — and there is enough evidence in his game to believe he handles that step up.

Miller compiled 20.2 points, 4.9 rebounds, and 3.3 assists in 65 games last year — while managing a shoulder injury. As the clear first option this season with the roster constructed specifically around him, everything should improve. The only question is whether the shoulder cooperates from day one.

Prediction: 23.5 points, 5.5 rebounds, 3.5 assists, 39.5% from three, 44% from the field

The leap from second option to franchise player is real, and this is where Miller earns it. He is athletic, skilled, competitive, and enters a season built around him. If the shoulder holds, a first All-Star appearance is genuinely on the table — and these numbers would justify that conversation.

Reid averaged 13.6 points, 6.2 rebounds, 36.2% from three in 26.1 minutes with the Timberwolves while mainly coming off the bench. In Charlotte, the spacing around him is significantly better than what he had in Minnesota — Knueppel, White, Allen and O'Neale all stretch the floor — which should open up more of his game in the mid-range and at the rim.

Prediction: 14.5 points, 6.5 rebounds, 37.4% from three

Modest growth — nothing dramatic — because Reid is a known commodity who thrives within a system rather than dominating it. His value to this team is consistency and spacing. Fourteen and a half points and six-plus rebounds every night would be exactly what Charlotte needs from him.

Diabate produced 7.9 points, 8.7 rebounds, 1.0 blocks, and 63.1% from the field in 26 minutes while also earning the NBA Hustle Award. He is locked in at $2.4 million for this season. For anyone still sleeping on Diabate, those numbers are remarkable for that price.

Prediction: 8.5 points, 10.7 rebounds, 1.2 blocks, 62% from the field in 28 minutes

Diabate projects to get slightly more minutes this year as Hannes Steinbach continues to develop. The rebounding climbs because the spacing around him creates more opportunities to crash on the offensive end without his man trailing. Diabate quietly compiling a case for most cost-efficient starter in the league is not a stretch — and these numbers would make that argument convincingly.

The Last Word on Hornets Starters Stats Projection

Add those predictions together, and Charlotte has a starting five capable of putting serious pressure on defenses, especially with Miller and Knueppel taking on larger offensive roles while White controls the offense.

The question hanging over all five projections is the same one that hangs over the season itself — health. Every one of these numbers requires the player in question to stay on the floor consistently. Miller's shoulder remains the obvious concern, and every projection assumes these players can stay on the floor consistently.

But if even four of the five stay healthy and hit these numbers, Charlotte gives themselves a genuine shot at ending that playoff drought.

Which starter do you think will have the biggest breakout? Drop your prediction in the comments.

articles.title: Athletes and Twitter sports lawyers got the Protect College Sports Act passed
articles.summary: Fans wanted the chaos to stop, and the source of the chaos pushed so far that fans finally got their wish.
articles.body:
It should surprise exactly no one that players, who were out of eligibility under NCAA rules, going through NFL training camp and filing lawsuits to play college football for another year was the last straw.

A week later, the Protect College Sports Act, dead in the water a month ago, is close to passing the Senate because the chaos finally got to be too much. It is, according to Team Chaos, bad for athletes.

This is what happens when you make everybody despise you.

When your position is that you have to have megaconferences, more hoarding of revenue by the conferences at the top, a stupid college basketball Thanksgiving week event in Las Vegas backed by all the worst people in existence (the Emiratis and David Ellison chief among them), more private equity backing, more helmet games, unlimited transfers, unlimited tampering with mid-major rosters, unlimited college eligibility and freedom to go back and forth between college and the pros as you please, all so that athletes can maximize their earnings …

…ultimately, fans decided that they didn't want athletes to be allowed to maximize their earnings. People who liked ten-team regional conferences, the Maui Invitational, four-year players who stayed at their school long enough for fans to know who they were, marching bands instead of DJs and light shows, and mid-major Cinderellas in March Madness learned that the athletes and their Sports Law Twitter advocates were fighting to destroy all of that so that they could make more money.

Advocates complained that athletes didn't have a seat at the table. The thing was that athletes did have a seat at the table, in the form of constant lawsuits and injunctions to handcuff the NCAA from enforcing any rules. That they used their seat at the table to completely turn public opinion against their position is the fault of the hubris of people who saw the NCAA unable to enforce the most basic of rules and decided to go for the jugular, assuming that they could hold the system hostage until they could force a new social contract on the sport. They were betting on Congress being so hopelessly divided that it could not wrangle enough votes for a bill. They were hoping Greg Sankey and Tony Pettiti would pressure Senators who represent the states in their conferences could go to bat for them, since of course the SEC and Big Ten share some (though not all) of the athletes' interests.

Instead, they flipped public opinion against their cause. Whatever Darren Heitner doesn't like about the PCSA is included because Darren Heitner doesn't like it. Congratulations, nobody likes you. Fans won with the PCSA, and now if we can get the maximum conference size down to 10…

articles.title: 4 bold predictions for Bears at Panthers
articles.summary: A strong start and a big day for the 2025 draft picks highlight our bold predictions for Bears vs. Panthers.
articles.body:
The 2026 regular season is just a few days away from beginning for the Chicago Bears as they make their final preparations before heading to Charlotte to take on the Carolina Panthers . It's a battle of two surprise division winners from a year ago, with each team hoping to get a jump start to the season.

For the Bears , they officially turned a corner last year during Ben Johnson's first season as head coach, becoming a dangerous team loaded on offense with talented pass catchers and a punishing rushing attack. And they were spearheaded by quarterback Caleb Williams , who broke out as the prolific playmaker he was billed as during his collegiate days to lead them to an 11-6 record atop the NFC North. The Bears advanced to the divisional round of the playoffs last year and are hoping to take another step in 2026 as contenders.

The Panthers, meanwhile, are coming off a successful season of their own under head coach Dave Canales. Carolina was able to hang around .500 all year long with some big wins against playoff contenders and eventually overtook the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to win the NFC South at 8-9. Quarterback Bryce Young took steps towards showing he can be a competent NFL quarterback, in part thanks to weapons such as Tetairoa McMillan , but he's entering a critical year in 2026.

Week 1 can feel like an outlier at times considering how much things can change between now and December. Look at what happened last year with Minnesota Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy . But we're sure to see some big moments on Sunday that turn the tide one way or another. Here are our bold predictions for Bears vs. Panthers.

1. Bears march down the field to score on their opening drive

For all of the talk of the Bears starting slow last season, they got off to hot starts early in the season. The game script was working for Ben Johnson and the offense, even when things still weren't totally clicking yet. In Weeks 1 and 2, they opened the game scoring on their first possession. Johnson has had time to game plan for the Panthers and will be ready with a systematic drive to score six early on.

With a heavy dose of the rushing attack and key conversions from Williams, the Bears will score a touchdown on their first possession to (hopefully) take the early lead. As for who will be the first player to reach the end zone? It has to be the newly-extended D'Andre Swift on a run to the right side.

2. Colston Loveland and Tetairoa McMillan each have 100-yard days

This Week 1 matchup is not only a meeting between Williams and Young as former No. 1 overall picks, but it's also a chance for two top-10 picks from the 2025 draft to meet for the first time. Tetairoa McMillan (No. 8 overall) and Colston Loveland (No. 10 overall) were two of the best rookie pass catchers last year. McMillan became a top target for Young and earned NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year honors, while Loveland finished the year strong as one of the most dangerous players at his position.

These two big-bodied targets will be busy for much of the day as go-to options for their respective teams. McMillan is easily the best pass catcher on the Panthers and with the Bears' secondary concerns, he's a threat to have a monster day. The same goes for Loveland, who has developed excellent chemistry with Williams and has ascended to become a No. 1 option as well. Each player will flex their muscles with 100 receiving-yard days in the blistering Carolina heat.

3. Montez Sweat gets two sacks and a tackle for loss

Have you noticed that seemingly every year in recent memory, a different Bears defensive lineman goes gangbusters in Week 1 with a star performance? There was Dominique Robinson in 2022, Yannick Ngakoue in 2023, Darrell Taylor in 2024, and even Dayo Odeyingbo in 2025. Each player had standout games early on, which means the tradition has to continue with someone else. How about Montez Sweat as he goes up against a rookie right tackle?

Sweat will be going up against rookie tackle Monroe Freeling, who has looked solid so far in Panthers camp, but has also been taken advantage of by upper echelon defensive linemen in joint practices. While Sweat may not be the best of the best, he's still very good and has a variety of tools at his disposal. The tested veteran will come out on top with a big day that includes multiple sacks and at least one tackle for loss against Freeling.

4. Bryce Young throws multiple interceptions

The concerns about the Bears defense going into 2026 have been talked about ad nauseum and while many of them are warranted, we shouldn't expect them to stop taking away the ball. Especially against a quarterback like Young. While the 2023 No. 1 overall pick took steps last year, one of his biggest issues still remains and that's starting the season out on the right foot.

Since coming into the league, Young is 0-3 in Week 1, has thrown two touchdowns to six interceptions, has averaged around 150 passing yards, and has a combined passer rating of 44.2. He's a slow starter and is prone to turnovers to start the season. Even with the defensive concerns, the Bears will pick off Young twice to add to those early-season struggles.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham Draws Hard Line After Enes Kanter Freedom Tries to Attach Her Name to His Campaign
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever are 26-14 with four games left in the regular season and home-court advantage on the line, so the last thing Sophie Cunningham wants to tal...
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever are 26-14 with four games left in the regular season and home-court advantage on the line, so the last thing Sophie Cunningham wants to talk about is Enes Kanter Freedom. The veteran guard has been one of the more outspoken players in the WNBA this summer on the topic of biological women in sports, but she is drawing a clear line between her own views and his courtside theatrics.

Cunningham was asked directly about Kanter Freedom and Royce White declaring themselves eligible for the WNBA draft, and her answer was short and simple. She wants no part of the circus.

Sophie Cunningham separates herself from Enes Kanter Freedom's campaign

Kanter Freedom and White drew attention after declaring themselves eligible for the WNBA draft. Kanter Freedom later attended a Fever game against the Chicago Sky wearing a shirt tied to his protest. He was ejected after a courtside exchange with Chicago guard Natasha Cloud .

Kanter Freedom also tried to connect his campaign to Cunningham's previous comments about biological women's sports. Cunningham has not backed away from that view, but she does not want her name used to promote someone else's public effort.

She addressed the issue as the Fever approach the final weeks of the regular season. Indiana holds a 26-14 record with four regular-season games left, leaving little room for distractions as the team fights for home-court advantage.

"I'm gonna let them do them,"Cunningham said . "I'm just focused on the Fever and on our sport. I think we have four more games left. I'm trying to just really dial in and keep the main thing the main thing."

She separated her personal views from Kanter Freedom's stunt and moved the focus back to basketball. The Fever now have to turn that focus into wins before the playoffs begin.

Fever face a demanding finish to the regular season

Cunningham has become a useful piece for Indiana because she brings outside shooting, toughness, and energy off the bench. She averages 8.3 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 1.3 assists, giving the Fever an option when starters need a break.

Indiana enters its final four regular-season games with a 26-14 record and home-court advantage at stake. Cunningham identified the Fever's biggest problems as poor defensive communication, rebounding, and rotations. Those issues matter more now because one weak stretch could change Indiana's playoff position.

The Fever need Cunningham's scoring and defensive effort through the finish. Cunningham must now translate her defensive critiques into on-court execution as Indiana locks into its final four regular-season matchups to secure playoff positioning.

articles.title: Lazio 2-2 AC Milan: Moreira Ends Gattuso’s Perfect Start in a Tale of Two Halves
articles.summary: At the Stadio Olimpico in Rome, Lazio squandered a two-goal lead as they registered a draw against AC Milan, who ended the Biancocelesti’s perfect Serie A re...
articles.body:
At the Stadio Olimpico in Rome, Lazio squandered a two-goal lead as they registered a draw against AC Milan , who ended the Biancocelesti's perfect Serie A record.

Gennaro Gattuso made three changes to his 4-3-3 starting lineup, with Tijjani Noslin leading the attack instead of Andrea Pinamonti , flanked by Mattia Zaccagni and Matteo Cancellieri , who came in for Gustav Isaksen . The manager also gave Josip Sutalo his Lazio debut due to Danilho Doekhi's injury .

The Croatian joined Romano Floriani Mussolini , Oliver Provstgaard , and Nuno Tavares in the backline, while Davide Frattesi , Reda Belahyane , and Kenneth Taylor constituted the midfield trio.

On the opposite side of the pitch, Ruben Amorim maintained his 3-4-2-1 system, spearheaded by Goncalo Ramos . The Portuguese striker was supported by Ruben Loftus-Cheek and Alphadjo Cisse, with Luka Modric and Adrien Rabiot occupying the double pivot. Samuel Chukwueze and Pervis Estupinan acted as wing-backs, while Mario Gila joined Koni De Winter and Strahinja Pavlovic at the back.

Straight after the kickoff, the two sides threw caution to the wind, with both teams keen on opening the lead. Milan drew first blood when Modric found Chukwueze with a delicate cross. The Nigerian's header was directed to the bottom corner, but Christos Mandas pulled off a superb reaction save.

Afterwards, it was all Lazio, with Taylor running the show. The Dutch midfielder found Zaccagni with a lovely through ball, but the captain's angle was too acute to beat Maignan . Taylor then released Floriani on the right flank, and the full-back fed Noslin with an inch-perfect square ball, but the latter should have done better in front of goal, as his shot was too central to trouble the Milan goalkeeper.

After a couple of warnings, the Biancocelesti seized the lead in the 10th minute from an excellent play launched by Tavares, who found a channel in the centre of the pitch and pushed forward before finding Zaccagni on the left side of the box.

Gila gave his former captain just enough time and space to deliver a square ball across the face of the goal. Cancellieri's connection wasn't the purest, but he only had to direct it into the empty net.

The Aquile almost gave away their lead cheaply due to a poor pass from Mandas, but Belahyane came to the rescue by denying Ramos a shooting opportunity.

Two minutes later, Lazio almost doubled their lead instantly with another gorgeous play. Noslin cut it back to Frattesi, who put Zaccagni through on goal, but Maignan raced off his line to produce an astonishing save and keep Milan in the game. Frattesi then almost scored his fourth of the season as he tried to find the far corner from a difficult angle, but his attempt whistled past the post.

Lazio eventually rounded off a superb first-half display with a well-deserved second goal. Zaccagni, Tavares, and Taylor combined on the left wing, and the latter tried to feed his Dutch compatriot Noslin with a square ball that caused a major goalmouth scramble.

The ball deflected off Estupinan and into the post. De Winter tried to clear it, but his shot hit Noslin, who was brave enough to put his face in the path, and was repaid with his first goal of the campaign.

Diego Moreira Scores Twice in Two Minutes

After the break, the visitors took the initiative following a triple substitution from Amorim, who brought in Christian Pulisic , Yunus Musah , and, more importantly, Diego Moreira. The Rossoneri dominated possession as Lazio retreated into their own areas. Mandas made two solid saves on Pavlovic and Pulisic, but was finally beaten by Moreira.

In the 65th minute, the Belgian wing-back got on the end of a cross from Chukwueze and smashed a volley from a tight angle. The powerful shot went through the Lazio goalkeeper's legs and into the net. Two minutes later, Moreira completed his brace after receiving a back pass from Rabiot into his stride. The new Milan signing struck the ball first time, expertly placing it in the far corner to restore parity.

Afterwards, the two sides seemed content to share the spoils, with neither relentlessly pushing for a winner, even though Moreira tried to complete a hat-trick from an impossible angle. Omari Hutchinson also tested Mandas with a long-range effort in the final minute of the game, but it was too central to trouble the Greek international.

At the final whistle, Milan were obviously the more satisfied team after cutting a two-goal deficit. On the other hand, Lazio will rue a poor second-half performance that cost them two points, but Gattuso's men continue to exceed expectations, as they temporarily climb to the top of the Serie A table while awaiting the rest of the weekend's results.

MILAN (3-4-2-1) : Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Pavlović; Chukwueze, Modrić (45′ Musah), Rabiot, Estupiñan (45′ Moreira); Loftus-Cheek (45′ Pulisic), Cissé (77′ Hutchinson); Ramos (85′ Camarda).

articles.title: Glasner praises players’ reaction to late changes due to injury blows after Nottingham Forest beat Aston Villa
articles.summary: Oliver Glasner has revealed Nottingham Forest were dealt a late double injury blow after Nikola Milenković and Jair Cunha were ruled out of their win over As...
articles.body:
Oliver Glasner has revealed Nottingham Forest were dealt a late double injury blow after Nikola Milenković and Jair Cunha were ruled out of their win over Aston Villa.

Both centre-backs had trained ahead of the game but complained of hamstring tightness, with scan results confirming at around the night before the match that neither would be able to feature.

"Yesterday we had the circumstances when we got the results of the scans at 9.30 in the evening and all of a sudden both centre-backs couldn't play," Glasner said.

"I knocked at Ola's and Ousmane's door and told them they will start in a back three.

"We had a lot of challenges to overcome, which is why I'm very proud of the performance and of the win."

Glasner was forced to reshuffle his defence at short notice, handing Ousmane Diomande an opportunity to come into the side.

"We trained yesterday, but it is how it is," he added. "We can't change it anymore and we trust in the other players.

"This is why we need the entire squad and it gives a chance to Ousmane. We are flexible and this is why we don't have doubts."

Liam Delap scored his first goal for the club in the victory before Igor Jesus struck a late winner after the home side had equaliser.

articles.title: DFS - Fantasy Domination Primetime Slate - Week 1
articles.summary: Breaking down the top DFS plays for DraftKings, FanDuel, and Fanball for the Week 1 Primetime Slate
articles.body:
DK Lineup : QB Dak Prescott ($6.4k), RB Javonte Williams ($6.3k), RB Cam Skattebo ($5.8k), WR CeeDee Lamb ($7.4k), WR Malik Nabers ($6.8k), WR Courtland Sutton ($6.0k), TE Isaiah Likely ($4.3k), FLEX Travis Kelce ($4.0k), DST Denver Broncos ($2.9k)

FD Lineup : QB Dak Prescott ($8.3k), RB Javonte Williams ($7.0k), RB Cam Skattebo ($6.5k), WR George Pickens ($8.3k), WR Malik Nabers ($7.9k), WR Jaylen Waddle ($6.3k), TE Isaiah Likely ($5.3k), FLEX Travis Kelce ($5.5k), DST Denver Broncos ($4.8k)

Dak Prescott (QB1) and Jaxson Dart (QB2) are the safe plays on this slate. Bo Nix (QB3) and Patrick Mahomes (QB4) make legitimate alternatives, but their opposing defenses are elite. If I had to choose one, it would be Nix. Fortunately, I don't have to choose either of them.

This week, I am also targeting the two running backs in the Giants -Cowboys tilt. Javonte Williams (RB1) is the top option on this slate. You can't fade him. RB2 is closer; I am leaning Cam Skattebo (RB2) over Kenneth Walker III (RB3), because of the price difference and their matchup. I don't want any part of the three-headed fool's errand that is the Denver backfield. J.K. Dobbins (RB4) is the best talent there, but the team intends to split the workload between him and R.J. Harvey (RB5). Harvey gets all the passing game work, making him a better option than Dobbins on DK. The team also intends to mix in rookie Jonah Coleman (RB7). Denver believes Coleman can get the job done both between the tackles and through the air, but this only earns him handcuff-level value without an injury to either Harvey or Dobbins.

The Giants have three proven veteran backups to Skattebo: Najee Harris (RB8), Tyrone Tracy Jr. (RB11) and Devin Singletary (RB12).When you have three backups ... you have zero backups. I cannot see starting any of them. With that said, Harris may have some Showdown value. Training camp darling Emmett Johnson (RB9) won the RB2 job in KC. He won't see significant touches this season without an injury. You can ignore him here. Malik Davis (RB13 - hip) won the backup job for the Cowboys in the preseason; unfortunately, he was carted off the practice field on Friday and appears likely to miss significant time. His injury will elevate Emari Demercado (RB10) into the depth rotation. Demercado had a few decent games for Arizona earlier in his career, but he only has Showdown value here.

You'd need to be insane to not roster one of the two Dallas starting receivers. CeeDee Lamb (WR1) and George Pickens (WR2) rank one and two on this slate. Rostering both would be difficult, but not impossible. It comes down to whether you want to get Malik Nabers (WR3 - knee) in your lineup at WR2. My preference is playing one of the Cowboys paired with Nabers. The pivot options would be either Jaylen Waddle (WR4) or Courtland Sutton (WR5). You can also consider one of them at WR3. Between those two, I would lean Waddle. Denver's pass defense is elite, so you can fade both Rashee Rice (WR6) and Xavier Worthy (WR7). I'd actually rather play Darnell Mooney (WR8), Marvin Mims Jr. (WR9) or Troy Franklin (WR10)

If I don't go spend-crazy at WR3/FLEX, I am leaning Franklin, Malachi Fields (WR11), Ryan Flournoy (WR12) or Odell Beckham Jr. (WR13). Pat Bryant (WR14) and Tyquan Thornton (WR15) are better best-ball plays than DFS plays. Both have Showdown value, but this is not the place to get cute with them. Cyrus Allen (WR16) flashed dominance this preseason, but he won't see the field without multiple injuries. Consider him useless at this point.

We have three very good tight ends on this docket (and they are all reasonably priced). I'm going to lean in favor of Isaiah Likely (TE1) and Travis Kelce (TE2), but Jake Ferguson (TE3) is certainly in play. This is also my favorite way to target the FLEX position this week. Using double-tight end opens the door to potentially use Lamb, Nabers and Waddle at WR. Sean Payton tends to ignore the tight end position. You should ignore his tight ends as well. Evan Engram (TE5) and Adam Trautman (TE6) are, at best, Showdown dart throws. I'd even use Theo Johnson (TE4) and possibly Noah Gray (TE7) before them.

I abhor cheering against the Chiefs, but Mahomes is coming off a major leg injury, and he is facing the frightening Broncos' defense. They are the best option on the defense board, and the price is reasonable. The Chiefs' defense is the only logical pivot, since their game will have less scoring than the NFC East tilt.e is facing the frightening Broncos' defense. articles.title: Cubs reinstate right-hander Edward Cabrera, move him to bullpen
articles.summary: The Chicago Cubs reinstated right-hander Edward Cabrera from the 15-day injured list before Saturday's game against the Pittsburgh Pirates and placed righty...
articles.body:
CHICAGO (AP) — The Chicago Cubs reinstated right-hander Edward Cabrera from the 15-day injured list before Saturday's game against the Pittsburgh Pirates and placed righty Trent Thornton on the 15-day IL with a left ankle sprain.

Cabrera went on the injured list on Aug. 17 with a right middle finger blister — a condition that has vexed him — then made three rehab appearances with Triple-A Iowa.

The 28-year-old Cabrera, acquired from Miami in an offseason trade, is 5-5 with a 5.68 ERA in 76 innings over 15 games, all starts. Manager Craig Counsell said before Saturday's game against Pittsburgh that Cabrera would switch to the bullpen for now.

This was Cabrera's third stint on the IL this season and followed one for a left hamstring/adductor strain suffered on June 23 in New York. The righty was hurt against the Mets when he went into the splits while stretching for a throw as he covered first base, an injury that sidelined Cabrera for nearly two months.

Thornton is 5-5 with three saves and 3.35 ERA in 48 1/3 innings over 48 relief appearances.

articles.title: ‘Can’t be happy’ – Iraola makes Liverpool admission following Fulham draw
articles.summary: Andoni Iraola admitted that Liverpool’s attack was not good enough after they were held to a goalless draw by Fulham at Anfield on Saturday. Despite apparent...
articles.body:
Andoni Iraola admitted that Liverpool 's attack was not good enough after they were held to a goalless draw by Fulham at Anfield on Saturday.

Despite apparent discontent in the Cottagers' squad, the visitors looked the more cohesive unit and created a number of openings on the day.

Josh King was at the centre of everything Fulham did in the final third, including their best chance of the match. An errant pass from Alisson Becker was pounced on by the opposition's high press, and in the Brazilian's desperation to atone for the mistake he almost wiped out the youngster. Gonzalo Garcia did get a shot off, but it was cleared off the line by Jeremy Jacquet .

Victor Munoz almost broke the deadlock but his header form a corner crashed off the crossbar. Liverpool were improved in the second half, but Alvaro Arbeloa's side held on for their first point of the season.

Iraola makes Liverpool admission following Fulham draw

Speaking after the full-time whistle, Iraola felt his side were not only poor in the final third, but also lacking in energy.

"When you draw, especially at home, you can't be happy," he told BBC Match of the Day. "Today we lacked a bit of freshness and we did not do enough offensively to make the difference.

"We have been good enough to keep the clean sheet. It was slightly better in the second half. In the first half we started the game slow, we lacked energy and it was not enough, we have to be offensively better."

Iraola made three changes to the side that beat Ipswich Town last weekend, with Milos Kerkez , Alexis Mac Allister and Cody Gakpo , who was carrying a knock, all dropping to the bench after Liverpool played Atletico Madrid in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday.

"It is less than three days, 60 hours, and a lot of players had to adapt," he said. "Most of the changes were for physical reasons because the players were tired, but that is the season and in less than three days we will be here against Spurs [in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday].

"We have to adapt and find ways to win."

Bradley Barcola had a quiet afternoon on his first Premier League start since joining Liverpool from PSG in a £123 million transfer, taking just one shot and creating one chance before coming off in the 72nd minute.

"Bradley is one we are building up physically with games and the games will give him the condition we want. But it is not just Bradley, we lack the freshness. I only remember one clear chance [for Fulham] and we kept the structure but offensively we need to do much better."

articles.title: Dodgers on Deck: Sunday, September 13 at Marlins
articles.summary: The Dodgers and Marlins conclude their 2026 business on Sunday afternoon at loanDepot Park in Miami. The Dodgers haven’t listed a starter, but Emmet Sheehan...
articles.body:
The Dodgers and Marlins conclude their 2026 business on Sunday afternoon at loanDepot Park in Miami.

The Dodgers haven't listed a starter, but Emmet Sheehan is in line to pitch bulk innings after his stellar Monday start at home. Justin Wrobleski was previously listed as the Sunday starter, perhaps as an opener, as the left-hander was also warming up to potentially pitch on Friday night in relief in Miami. There's also when the Dodgers decide to activate Roki Sasaki off the injured list to consider.

Right-hander Eury Pérez starts for Miami.

Radio: AM 570 (English), KTNQ 1020 AM (Spanish)

articles.title: Kids evade security, entertain crowd during Kansas State, Wazzu weather delay
articles.summary: Two kids turned a K-State weather delay into must-see entertainment, evading security and drawing cheers from the crowd at Bill Snyder Family Stadium.
articles.body:
MANHATTAN — A pair of children ran on the field and evaded security during a weather delay at halftime of Kansas State 's matchup with Washington State on Saturday, Sept. 12.

A child in white and another in Wazzu maroon entertained the crowd as they waited for play to resume. The kiddo in maroon lasted the longest , running across the entire field before cutting back to run in front of the K-State student section.

After the kid in maroon was caught, the Kansas State student section cheered for someone wearing Cougars clothing all afternoon.

Kansas State led 17-7 at halftime. The second half was close to beginning before a lightning strike put the game on delay. The Cougars scored their touchdown on a 50-yard interception return on the final play of the first half.

The Wildcats' defense has held the Cougars to 84 yards at the break. Avery Johnson has completed 14 of 22 passes for 134 yards, two touchdowns and two picks. Josh Manning has seven catches for 52 yards and a score.

See our best photos from Kansas State football vs Washington State in Week 2

articles.title: How Many Games Will the Dolphins Win This Season?
articles.summary: What experts, markets and models think about Miami’s chances
articles.body:
Did you know the American lobster has a lifespan of about 15 years? That's also the average lifespan of goats, cows, female lions and the small parrot known as the budgie. If you considered all of the lobsters, goats, cows, lionesses and budgies born in 2010, they will have lived their entire natural lives, all fifteen years, having witnessed only a single winning season from the New York Jets.*

Admittedly, the Miami Dolphins aren't looking that hot right now either, and we have our own streak of futility that we don't need to get into here. But there's a difference between a bad team and an unproven team, and right now, the Dolphins have so many question marks at every position (including the head coach) that they're hard to quantify. They're the NFL's youngest team, so you have to assume growing pains, but are they Jets-level bad?

Since we're right on the cusp of the 2026 regular season, here are what various prognosticators are predicting for the Dolphins' win total in 2026. I'll offer my own take at the end, but throw your guesses in the comments.

Good Morning Football's Peter Schrager: 5 wins

I know I tend to view the Dolphins with aqua-and-orange-tinted glasses, but I think the team's offense has some real juice. The depth is a little scary, though, and I think like a quarter of the team just signed two weeks ago. Plus with so many first- and second-year players, it might look a bit ugly at times, especially early on. But you can put me down for 6 wins as the first step in a successful rebuild.

How do you see the team finishing this year? Share your thoughts in the comments!

*And to all those elderly lobsters and budgies born in 2011 hoping this is the Jets' year: Don't hold your breath.
